metadata.note: The North Carolina Railroad's Charlotte-Greensboro-Raleigh corridor, leased and operated by the Southern Railway, the historical line underlying Amtrak's Piedmont and the western portion of its Carolinian. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The North Carolina Railroad, chartered 1849, opened Greensboro-Goldsboro Dec 13 1855 and Greensboro-Charlotte Jan 30 1856, completing a 223-mile Goldsboro-Raleigh-Greensboro-Salisbury-Charlotte corridor. It is largely responsible for the 'Piedmont Urban Crescent' of cities that grew along it, including Durham, Burlington and High Point. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
